summary: Lehner's Heit el-Ghurab 'Workers Town' analysis: no evidence for regular national corvée or captive foreigners as labor source; workers organized into crews (aprw), phyles (zAw), divisions.
content: The Heit el-Ghurab (HeG) settlement at Giza. Evidence of abundant meat, hunted game, Levantine luxury imports suggests either good treatment of common workers or higher-status occupants. Conclusion: no evidence for a regular, out-of-district, national corvée, nor for captive foreigners as a labor source for pyramid building. Workers organized into crews/gangs (aprw), phyles (zAw), and divisions. The site may have been a Nile port/entrepôt. Defeats a simple dichotomy of elite and non-elite.
